_note: A holiday list is a safety device, and a wrong one is worse than an absent
one: a date this file gets wrong is a day the engine either sits out a live
session or, far worse, tries to trade a closed exchange and spends the
morning interpreting silence as a quiet tape.
So these dates were NOT written from memory. See `_provenance` below.
What the engine does with it (src/ose/risk.js — validateCalendar):
* empty or unreadable  -> refuses to start in production, warns elsewhere
* no date on or after today in the current year -> treated as STALE, same
refusal. A calendar that ran out in December is a calendar nobody
maintained. THIS FILE GOES STALE ON 2026-12-26 — replace it before then.
* weekends are detected from the IST day of week and are NOT listed here.
Format: either a plain 'YYYY-MM-DD' string or { date, name }. Both are
accepted so the list can carry the holiday's name without a second file.
The key is `holidays`. `dates` is also accepted (src/ose/risk.js —
readCalendar), because an earlier revision of this note asked for `dates`
while every reader took `holidays`, and a calendar filled in as instructed
_provenance: Compiled 2026-08-02. Two steps, because the year-to-date half of a calendar
is a FACT that can be checked and the forward half is not.
1. OBSERVED. NIFTY daily bars for 2026-01-01..2026-08-02 were pulled from
Yahoo (^NSEI) and every weekday with no bar was taken as a closed day.
That yielded exactly ten dates — an empirical record of when the
exchange was actually shut, derived without consulting any holiday list.
2. SOURCED. The full-year list was then taken from two independent
published calendars (see _sources) and checked against those ten:
observed but missing from the list  0   <- the dangerous direction
Exact agreement on the verifiable half. That is what the forward dates
rest on; they are not independently verifiable until they arrive.
NOT ASSERTED: the holiday NAMES below come from the same sources and were
not separately checked. Nothing in the engine reads them — only `date`.
Independence Day (2026-08-15) and three other notified holidays fall on
weekends in 2026 and are deliberately absent: risk.isWeekend covers them.
_disputed: 2026-11-24 (Guru Nanak Jayanti) appears in the Kotak Neo list and NOT in
the ClearTax one. It is INCLUDED here deliberately.
The two errors are not symmetric. Listing a day that turns out to trade
costs one sat-out session. Omitting a day that turns out to be shut means
the engine opens a naked short into an exchange that cannot fill or close
it. Confirm against the NSE circular before November and remove it if the
exchange is open — but until then, closed is the safe assumption.
